quizzes.title: Storybook Favourites
quizzes.description: Much-loved children's books and the unforgettable characters inside them.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland'?
questions.note: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, an Oxford mathematician.

questions.q: Winnie-the-Pooh was created by A. A. Milne.
questions.note: Pooh was based on Christopher Robin Milne's teddy, named after a London Zoo bear called Winnipeg.

questions.q: In Roald Dahl's famous book, what is the name of the chocolate factory owner?
questions.note: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory was published in 1964.

questions.q: What is the name of J. M. Barrie's boy who never grows up?
questions.note: Barrie gave the rights to Peter Pan to Great Ormond Street Hospital in 1929.

questions.q: What kind of animal is Aslan in The Chronicles of Narnia?
questions.note: Narnia's author, C. S. Lewis, was a close friend of J. R. R. Tolkien.

questions.q: Who wrote and illustrated 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar'?
questions.note: The Very Hungry Caterpillar was first published in 1969.

questions.q: Harry Potter's pet owl is called Crookshanks.
questions.note: Harry's owl is Hedwig; Crookshanks is Hermione's cat.

questions.q: Which Dr. Seuss character stole Christmas?
questions.note: How the Grinch Stole Christmas! was published in 1957.

questions.q: Which bear from 'darkest Peru' lives with the Brown family in London?
questions.note: Michael Bond's first Paddington book came out in 1958.

questions.q: What happens to Pinocchio's nose when he tells a lie?
questions.note: Carlo Collodi's Italian story was first serialised between 1881 and 1883.

quizzes.title: Famous Faces of Fiction
quizzes.description: Detectives, villains and heroes from the classic novels everyone has heard of.

questions.q: Agatha Christie's detective Hercule Poirot comes from which country?
questions.note: Poirot first appeared in The Mysterious Affair at Styles.

questions.q: Sherlock Holmes's loyal friend and chronicler is Dr Watson.
questions.note: Holmes and Watson first appeared in A Study in Scarlet in 1887.

questions.q: In Jane Austen's 'Pride and Prejudice', whom does Elizabeth Bennet marry?
questions.note: Mr Darcy's first name is Fitzwilliam.

questions.q: Who is the narrator of 'The Great Gatsby'?
questions.note: F. Scott Fitzgerald published The Great Gatsby in 1925.

questions.q: In Robert Louis Stevenson's novella, what is the surname of Dr Jekyll's evil alter ego?
questions.note: Accept 'Mr Hyde'; the story was published in 1886.

questions.q: In Dickens's 'A Christmas Carol', what is Scrooge's first name?
questions.note: Jacob Marley was Scrooge's late business partner; Bob Cratchit was his clerk.

questions.q: In Mary Shelley's novel, Frankenstein is the name of the monster.
questions.note: Victor Frankenstein is the scientist; his creature is never given a name.

questions.q: Which author created the lawyer Atticus Finch?
questions.note: Atticus is the father of Scout in To Kill a Mockingbird (1960).

questions.q: What is the name of the dragon Bilbo Baggins faces in 'The Hobbit'?
questions.note: Smaug guarded the treasure of the Lonely Mountain, Erebor.

questions.q: In 'Treasure Island', what is the name of the one-legged ship's cook?
questions.note: Stevenson's Treasure Island was published as a book in 1883.

quizzes.title: Indian Literary Greats
quizzes.description: Epics, poets and prize-winning novelists from India's rich literary tradition.

questions.q: In which year did Rabindranath Tagore win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
questions.note: He was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

questions.q: What is the name of R. K. Narayan's fictional South Indian town?
questions.note: Malgudi first appeared in Narayan's debut novel, Swami and Friends (1935).

questions.q: Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize for 'The God of Small Things'.
questions.note: She won in 1997 with her debut novel.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel 'Midnight's Children'?
questions.note: It won the Booker Prize in 1981 and was later named the 'Booker of Bookers'.

questions.q: Which author, long based in Mussoorie, wrote 'The Blue Umbrella' and 'Rusty' stories?
questions.note: Accept 'Bond'; he has lived in Landour, Mussoorie, for decades.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Vande Mataram', India's national song?
questions.note: It appeared in his 1882 novel Anandamath.

questions.q: Which poet was known as the 'Nightingale of India'?
questions.note: Sarojini Naidu later became India's first woman state governor.

questions.q: Vikram Seth's 'A Suitable Boy' is a short novella of under 100 pages.
questions.note: At about 1,350 pages, it is one of the longest single-volume novels in English.

questions.q: Which Hindi writer, author of 'Godaan', is often called 'Upanyas Samrat'?
questions.note: Accept 'Premchand'; his real name was Dhanpat Rai Srivastava.

questions.q: Which classical poet wrote the Sanskrit play 'Abhijnanashakuntalam'?
questions.note: The play tells the love story of King Dushyanta and Shakuntala.

quizzes.title: First Lines & Famous Verses
quizzes.description: Name the novel from its opening line and the poet from their most famous verse.

questions.q: 'Mother died today. Or maybe yesterday; I can't be sure.' opens which novel?
questions.note: Albert Camus's L'Étranger (1942) is also published in English as The Outsider.

questions.q: 'Call me Ishmael.' is the opening line of which novel?
questions.note: Herman Melville's Moby-Dick was published in 1851.

questions.q: 'It is a truth universally acknowledged…' is the first line of Jane Austen's 'Emma'.
questions.note: That famous line opens Pride and Prejudice (1813).

questions.q: Who wrote the poem 'The Road Not Taken'?
questions.note: It was partly inspired by Frost's country walks with the poet Edward Thomas.

questions.q: Which poet wrote 'I wandered lonely as a cloud', the poem about daffodils?
questions.note: Accept 'William Wordsworth'; the poem was first published in 1807.

questions.q: 'Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way' opens which novel?
questions.note: Leo Tolstoy's Anna Karenina was published in book form in 1878.

questions.q: 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?' opens Shakespeare's sonnet number…
questions.note: Shakespeare's sonnets were published as a collection in 1609.

questions.q: 'It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen' opens which novel?
questions.note: Accept 'Nineteen Eighty-Four'; George Orwell published it in 1949.

questions.q: 'The Raven', with its refrain 'Nevermore', was written by Edgar Allan Poe.
questions.note: Poe published The Raven in 1845.

questions.q: Which poet wrote 'Do not go gentle into that good night'?
questions.note: Dylan Thomas wrote it for his dying father.
